items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: that’s how Mary got into it. And you know the story from then, it went like gangbusters.

ctx.x: Yeah, we were right at a break with the head of the thing, Joe was gone, and Dick had just come in and Dick came to see me in San Diego. And I explained to him this thing. And I said God it’s dead. I’m looking for another school to put it where it will get done. He said well let me try it. So he came back and that’s how Mary got into it. And you know the story from then, it went like gangbusters. And I was fortunate enough to convince you guys that you should go to jazz parties. Because Joe was going to go to…

not cooperate because they’d been taken to town so many times. So we had Joe, we had a meeting over at C&D with Joe, and I’m not sure you were there the first time. Mary and Joe and Dean I guess and me. And Joe agreed to help out. And so we got him to sign a letter that went to all the musicians saying these guys are for real, you can bank on it, don’t worry. And that’s what got you in. That’s why they agreed to be interviewed. So we owe a great deal to Joe. But he was all for it. And he loved the college, he…
